terms.meaning: the set of tables, columns, and rules that define a database's structure
a PostgreSQL tool that writes out a database's structure as SQL
a column or set of columns that uniquely identifies each row
a rule that stops two rows from having the same value in given columns
a lookup structure that makes searches on a column faster
a counter that hands out numbers, such as row ids
the list of places PostgreSQL looks for names when a statement does not give a full name
a value that means unknown or missing
a column type that stores structured data such as lists and objects
a rule that rejects a row whose values break a condition

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Header and dump settings
sections.what: Explains that this file is a full structure snapshot for an empty database, and that the migration files cannot be replayed from empty. It then sets the session options that PostgreSQL needs while loading.
sections.why: The header records why the snapshot exists. The session options are standard output of the dump tool.
sections.watch_out: The header says to apply it only to an empty database.

sections.name: SELECT
sections.title: Clearing the name search path
sections.what: Empties the list of places PostgreSQL searches for names, so each table name must be written in full, and sets a few standard options.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. It is standard dump output that makes name lookup exact.
sections.watch_out: Changing the search path can make later statements point at the wrong schema.

sections.name: CREATE

sections.what: Creates a separate namespace named drizzle to hold the migration bookkeeping, apart from the application tables.

summary: A full snapshot of the database layout (tables, keys, indexes and the migration ledger) for a new, empty PostgreSQL database, with no data.
purpose: Lets someone build a fresh database with the current structure in one step, instead of replaying the old incremental migrations.
why: The header says the migration files cannot be replayed from an empty database, so this snapshot is the end state of all of them.
how: The file first sets session options and clears the search path. It creates the drizzle schema and the migration ledger table, then creates each application table, then adds comments, then primary keys and unique rules, then indexes. The table list is in alphabetical order.
inputs: An empty PostgreSQL database. The header says it should be applied with the pnpm run db:schema command, which refuses to run on a non-empty database.
outputs: Tables, sequences, constraints, indexes and comments in the target database, plus the ledger rows.
risks: Running it against a database that already has tables will conflict or do damage. The header says a guard exists, but that command is not in the packet. Some values are only described in comments and are not enforced in the visible parts.
debug: If the apply fails, check that the database is empty and that the PostgreSQL version matches the one the dump came from. Look for the first error, since later errors often follow from it.
